web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers
question: At $71.37 per share ($14.20B market cap), what revenue growth, margin expansion, and TEU-diluted cash conversion is the market already pricing into BrightSpring Health Services—and how does its multiple stack up against specialty infusion and distribution peers?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. When a low-margin distributor trades at a high-margin multiple, the market is betting on mix shift and operating leverage that have not yet finished arriving.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk Principle

web_blocks.title: 7.1 Post-IPO Re-Rating: From $13.00 Debacle to $71.37 Compounder

web_blocks.html: BrightSpring's equity has staged a sharp post-IPO re-rating [16, 17]. It priced its January 26, 2024 IPO at $13.00 per share, closed day one at $11.00, and hit an $8.23 low in March 2024 [16, 17]. By November 16, 2026, shares reached $71.37—up 5.5x from the IPO and +128.02% over 12 months [16, 18]. At $71.37 on 198.81M basic shares, market cap is $14.20B and headline EV is $15.87B ($15.66B using Q3 2026 net debt of $1,464.3M) [2, 18].

A disciplined buyer must adjust for the February 1, 2027 conversion of 8.0M Tangible Equity Units (TEUs) [6]. Above the upper threshold, conversion adds ~26.2M shares, lifting diluted shares to ~225.0M [6]. Pro-forma market cap is ~$16.06B and pro-forma EV is ~$17.52B. On basic numbers, BTSG trades at 46.35x TTM P/E ($1.54 EPS), 28.73x Forward P/E, 29.04x P/FCF, 21.05x TTM EV/EBITDA, and 1.04x EV/Sales [18]. Against $850M–$860M FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance, EV/FY26E EBITDA is ~18.5x (~20.5x TEU-diluted) [2]. Wall Street's 100% Buy consensus averages $83.21, assuming smooth FY2027 margin expansion [15].

We invert the DCF at $71.37 ($16.06B TEU-diluted equity, 10.0% WACC, 3.0% terminal growth). FY2025 free cash flow was $394.7M, and FY2026E normalized FCF is ~$490M (~57% conversion on $855M Adjusted EBITDA) [1, 2]. At $71.37, the market prices in 14.5%–16.0% annual FCF growth for 10 years (reaching ~$1.9B–$2.1B in Year-10 FCF). Revenue must scale from $16.0B toward $32B+ while GAAP operating margin rises from 3.90% TTM toward 5.0%–5.5%.

web_blocks.title: 7.3 Peer Valuation Comparison: Paying a Growth Premium Over Pure-Play Peers

web_blocks.html: Against Option Care Health (OPCH), Addus HomeCare (ADUS), McKesson (MCK), and Cencora (COR), BTSG trades at a clear premium [18, 19, 20, 21, 22]. Its 28.73x Forward P/E and 21.05x EV/EBITDA exceed peers at 15.30x–21.14x Forward P/E and 12.48x–17.16x EV/EBITDA [18, 19, 20, 21, 22]. BTSG's 1.04x EV/Sales looks low only because high-priced specialty drugs pass through revenue at thin margins [18]. Analysts stay bullish on 26%+ sales growth, yet 28.7x leaves little room for error [2, 15].

Capital efficiency explains the gap with McKesson (76.71% ROIC) and Cencora (23.63% ROIC) [21, 22]. Drug wholesalers run on negative working capital. BrightSpring carries $3.10B of LBO-era goodwill and intangibles, holding ROIC at 7.58% [1, 18]. Meanwhile, OPCH (15.30x Forward P/E) and ADUS (16.26x Forward P/E) trade at 40%–45% discounts [19, 20]. To keep a 20x+ EV/EBITDA multiple, BTSG must lift incremental ROIC above 15% and absorb February 2027 TEU dilution [6].

A sum-of-the-parts check confirms this math. Valuing Pharmacy Solutions (~$720M FY26E EBITDA) at 17x–18x gives ~$12.6B EV, and Provider Services (~$135M EBITDA) at 13x–14x gives ~$1.8B EV [2, 3]. Totaling $14.4B EV implies ~$64–$65 basic ($57–$58 TEU-diluted) before any growth premium [6]. Still, bears focused only on 46.35x trailing GAAP P/E missed the deleveraging story [18]. As debt drops and interest expense falls below FY2025's $157.3M, GAAP earnings will converge toward cash flow [1]. That dynamic makes BTSG a genuine post-LBO deleveraging compounder whose price simply ran ahead of near-term support.
Valuation Change Trigger: A pullback to $64.56–$68.21 (~18.0x–19.0x TEU-diluted FY26E EBITDA) or FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA guidance above $1.05B would restore an asymmetric margin of safety.

web_blocks.text: Valuation Takeaway: BTSG is not cheap on trailing or forward earnings (28.73x Forward P/E; 21.05x TTM EV/EBITDA), and February 2027 TEU conversion adds ~26.2M shares. The multiple is justified only if LDD oncology launches and home health density sustain 15%+ multi-year EBITDA compounding—making entry price discipline critical.

book_paragraphs: Now that we have locked down BrightSpring's business quality without looking at the ticker tape, let's open the valuation ledger and ask the hardest question in investing: at $71.37 per share, what is the market already assuming?

Remember where this stock came from. When KKR and Walgreens brought BrightSpring public in January 2024 at $13.00 a share, institutional investors hated the leverage and complexity. The stock broke issue on day one, closing at $11.00, and sank to $8.23 in March 2024. Since then, management sold ResCare Community Living for $835 million, cut net leverage to 1.79x, and scaled oncology and infusion revenue past $15 billion. The market rewarded that execution with a 5.5x run from the IPO price.

At $71.37, you are no longer buying an ignored turnaround. On 198.81 million basic shares, the market cap is $14.20 billion, and once you account for the 26.2 million shares coming from the February 1, 2027 Tangible Equity Unit conversion, the true diluted equity value is roughly $16.06 billion. You are paying 28.73x forward earnings and roughly 20.5x diluted FY2026E Adjusted EBITDA for a business with a 3.90% trailing operating margin and a 7.58% headline ROIC.

Why does the market willingly pay 28.73x forward earnings for a 3.9% operating-margin business? Because Wall Street is looking through the consolidated revenue denominator to the gross profit dollar growth engine. When specialty oncology scripts grow 34% year-over-year and gross profit per script rises 27% to $28.86, incremental EBITDA drops through at a much higher rate than legacy long-term care dispensing.

Our Reverse DCF shows what that price demands over the next decade. Starting from roughly $490 million of normalized FY2026 free cash flow, $71.37 already bakes in 15.2% annual free cash flow growth for ten consecutive years—requiring revenue to double past $32 billion while operating margins expand from 3.9% toward 5.0%. That is a high bar for any healthcare services company, especially one that must fund $1.22 billion of accounts receivable as it grows.

Compare BrightSpring side-by-side with the pure-play peers in our table. Option Care Health, our moat-scaling twin in home infusion, trades at 15.30x forward earnings and 13.88x EV/EBITDA. Addus HomeCare trades at 16.26x forward earnings and 12.48x EV/EBITDA. Even McKesson, with a 76.7% ROIC and unmatched US Oncology distribution scale, trades at 21.14x forward earnings. Cencora trades at 16.43x. BrightSpring's 28.73x multiple is earned by its 26% top-line growth and 155+ limited-distribution drugs, but it leaves zero room for an IRA Part D stumble or a working-capital air pocket.

Think about what happens to a stock's multiple when a healthcare roll-up transitions from hyper-growth to normal 10%–12% EBITDA growth. If BrightSpring's forward P/E compresses from 28.7x down toward McKesson's 21.1x or Option Care's 15.3x, earnings have to grow 35% to 85% just to keep the share price flat. That is the exact valuation gravity we saw in our Reverse DCF: to earn a 15% annualized return from $71.37, BrightSpring cannot merely meet guidance—it must keep beating and raising while converting at least 55% to 60% of Adjusted EBITDA into true free cash flow.

There is also a technical equity-supply event sitting right on the calendar: February 1, 2027. On that date, the 8.0 million Tangible Equity Units issued during the January 2024 IPO mandatorily convert into at least 26.2 million common shares. Because BTSG trades far above the TEU upper conversion threshold, dilution is already mathematically locked in, yet retail quote screens still display the 198.81 million basic share count. Sophisticated institutional buyers price BTSG on the 225 million diluted share count—which means at $71.37, you are paying roughly $16.06 billion for the equity, not $14.20 billion. Recognizing that difference early keeps us from overpaying at the top of the range.

Let's also run a quick sum-of-the-parts sanity check so we don't rely solely on a ten-year DCF. If you value BrightSpring's Pharmacy Solutions engine at 17.5x FY2026E EBITDA—already a healthy premium to Option Care Health's 13.88x—and you value the Provider Services home health and rehab business at 13.5x, you arrive at roughly $14.4 billion of enterprise value. Subtracting $1.46 billion of net debt leaves about $12.9 billion of equity value, which translates to roughly $65 per basic share or $57 to $58 per TEU-diluted share. That simple napkin math explains why the $64.56–$68.21 zone is not just a technical moving-average shelf—it is where fundamental sum-of-the-parts support begins to kick in.

At the same time, I want you to understand why the short sellers—currently holding 6.87% of the float—have been run over since 2024. If you only screen on trailing GAAP P/E of 46.35x, BrightSpring looks absurdly expensive. Why is GAAP net income so much lower than Adjusted EBITDA? Because KKR's LBO left behind $558 million of amortizable intangibles and heavy interest expense. As BrightSpring pays down debt from 2.99x to 1.79x leverage, interest expense shrinks and GAAP net income catches up to cash flow. The business is genuinely deleveraging into its multiple; we just refuse to pay peak extension for it.

Let's also check what Wall Street analysts are modeling so we know where consensus sits relative to our own numbers. Across the Street, 100% of covering analysts rate BTSG a Buy or Outperform, with an average target of $83.21 and a high target of $92.00 to $96.60. Notice how closely our $83.00 base case aligns with the Street's $83.21 consensus—and notice what that means. There is no hidden catalyst that Wall Street has missed. To outperform from $71.37, BrightSpring either has to beat consensus again in 2027, or we have to buy the shares at a discount during a market-wide pullback.

One last valuation lens is worth keeping in your pocket: Enterprise Value to Sales. BrightSpring trades at just 1.04x trailing sales of $15.25 billion, which can fool casual observers into thinking the stock is cheap. Remember why EV/Sales is low: specialty oncology and infusion drugs carry huge ticket prices—often $10,000 to $20,000 per fill—that pass through BrightSpring's top line at a 12.5% gross margin. Never value a specialty pharmacy on EV/Sales; always anchor on EV-to-gross-profit, EV-to-EBITDA, and free cash flow conversion.

Put all four valuation lenses together—Reverse DCF, peer multiples, sum-of-the-parts, and TEU dilution—and a clear picture emerges. BrightSpring is not a broken roll-up, nor is it an undiscovered bargain. At $71.37, you are paying full institutional price for 2027 execution. If the market hands us a pullback into the mid-$60s, that same math flips decisively in our favor.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Never Confuse a Great Turnaround With a Cheap Entry
book_callouts.text: At $13 in 2024, BrightSpring was priced for balance-sheet distress. At $71.37 in late 2026, it is priced for near-flawless execution. That doesn't make the business bad—it means our entry price must build in a margin of safety.
